name.en: Fake purchase: “call us to cancel this payment”

how.en: A message says you bought something you didn’t, often for $300 to $2,000: a phone, security software, tickets or crypto. It looks like a PayPal invoice, a software renewal or an app receipt, may include your real name or address, and shows a phone number to call before the money is taken. The person who answers asks for your bank or card details “for a refund”, says they refunded too much, gets you to install software to control your device, or asks you to buy gift cards.

text.en: You get a receipt or invoice for something you didn’t buy, from a brand you know.
It says the money will be taken soon unless you call the number in the message.
On the call they ask you to install software so they can “process the refund”.
They ask for your card details, say they refunded too much, or ask for gift cards.
PayPal: Your payment of $1,489.99 AUD to Apple Store has been approved. If you did not make this purchase, call our support team within 24 hours to cancel.

en: buy gift cards to catch the scammers
A purchase or payment you don’t recognise.
A phone number shown clearly with instructions to call.
A high amount, often $300 or more, to make you worry.
Being asked to install software, buy gift cards or send money back.
Don’t call the number in the message.
Check the payment yourself in the official app or website.
Never install software or share one-time codes or gift card numbers on a call.

sources.title: Scam alert: Fake purchase callback scams
